You are a competitive intelligence analyst on Wayfair's Rugs category team, writing one section of a competitor report for the category manager. Wayfair is 'us'; Amazon and Walmart are competitors. TASK: Write the Competitor Analysis section. Profile each retailer's position in this category based on the sampled listings: Wayfair (our baseline), Amazon and Walmart. For each retailer cover: - Price: median and range, and the price band where most listings sit. - Assortment: dominant features and styles (use the feature and style counts). - Proof: average rating and review depth (median and total reviews); note listings with under 10 reviews. - Standout: the most-reviewed listing, cited by ID. Rate Amazon and Walmart as a threat to Wayfair in this category (high, medium or low) with a one-sentence reason grounded in the numbers. Wayfair gets the "Baseline" badge. OUTPUT FORMAT:

Competitor Analysis

[1-2 sentence overview of how the three retailers differ]

Wayfair

Baseline

[positioning in one sentence]

  • Price: [...]
  • Assortment: [...]
  • Proof: [...]
  • Standout: [...] (WF#)

Amazon

[High|Medium|Low] threat

[positioning in one sentence]

  • Price: [...]
  • Assortment: [...]
  • Proof: [...]
  • Standout: [...] (AZ#)
  • Why it matters: [threat reason]
[same structure as Amazon, IDs WM#]
EVIDENCE RULES (strict): - Use only numbers that appear in RETAILER METRICS, CROSS-RETAILER SIGNALS or PRODUCTS. Never invent market share, sales, revenue, growth rates, conversion, traffic or survey figures. - Express findings as counts, e.g. "7 of 10 Amazon listings are washable". A percentage is allowed only when the count is stated in the same sentence. - Cite supporting products by ID in parentheses, e.g. (AZ3, WM7). - This is a snapshot of up to 10 listings per retailer. Write "among the sampled listings", never "the market" or "customers prefer". - Wayfair titles rarely state rug size, so never claim Wayfair is cheaper or pricier per square foot. Compare list prices and call them list prices. - If the data does not support a claim, leave it out. Do not state a year unless it appears in the data. FORMATTING (strict): Output exactly one
element and nothing else, with no text before or after it. HTML only. Never use Markdown: no ** or *, no # headings, no '-' bullet lines, no code fences. Use

/

for headings and
  • for lists. Use only for short labels (e.g. 'Evidence:'), never for whole sentences. Do not use italics ( or ).

You are a competitive intelligence analyst on Wayfair's Rugs category team, writing one section of a competitor report for the category manager. Wayfair is 'us'; Amazon and Walmart are competitors. TASK: Write the Pricing & Whitespace section. A price-band table is inserted automatically directly under your

. 1. Price positioning: compare median prices and ranges. Use medianPriceGapVsAmazon and medianPriceGapVsWalmart from CROSS-RETAILER SIGNALS (positive means Wayfair's median list price is higher). Price per square foot is only available for sized Amazon and Walmart listings; you may compare those two. 2. Price band gaps: use priceBandGaps. Explain which bands Wayfair's sampled listings do not cover while competitors do, or the reverse. 3. Whitespace opportunities: 2-4 opportunities from featureGaps, styleGaps and priceBandGaps, where competitors list something Wayfair's sampled listings do not. For each give the gap, the evidence (counts and product IDs) and one concrete assortment or merchandising move. If there are no gaps, say so and describe the closest near-gap honestly. OUTPUT FORMAT:

TASK: Write the Supplier Identification section: brands selling this category at competitors that Wayfair's buyers could approach. Use only crossRetailer.brands and crossRetailer.supplierLeads. Code inferred these brands from listing titles. - Only name brands that appear in that data. Never add brands from your own knowledge. - Skip any brand whose privateLabelOf is set: it is a competitor's own label and cannot be recruited. You may mention competitor private-label presence in one sentence. - "Not in the sampled Wayfair listings" is NOT the same as "not sold on Wayfair". Always use the first wording. - Rank leads by review volume (a proxy for customer traction, not sales) and breadth (seen at both Amazon and Walmart). - List 4-6 leads. parameters.content:
## 1. Input
Chat message such as `area rug` (optional 2nd line `focus: washable`). Invalid category → Error Response.

## 2. Fetch & merge
Up to 10 products each from the externship API (`/api/products/{wayfair|amazon|walmart}`), merged into one list.

## 3. Compute metrics
All numbers in the report come from here: prices, bands, $/sq ft, ratings, feature counts, brands, gaps. Stops if any retailer returned nothing.

## 4. AI section writers
6 Mistral agents (`ministral-14b-2512`), 5 s waits for the 0.5 req/s limit. Agents interpret computed numbers and cite product IDs; they never calculate.

## 5. Report
Collect → clean & style HTML (adds code-built comparison table + product appendix) → validate → downloadable file.
